summary.text: John Sununu is the Republican nominee for the open New Hampshire U.S. Senate seat. A mechanical engineer and MBA who worked in engineering, consulting and manufacturing, he served in the U.S. House from 1997 to 2003 and in the Senate from 2003 to 2009, losing his 2008 re-election bid to Jeanne Shaheen. He announced this campaign in late 2025 for the seat Shaheen is vacating.

paragraphs.text: Born in Boston, Massachusetts, on September 10, 1964, one of eight siblings; son of former New Hampshire Gov. John H. Sununu (R) and brother of former Gov. Chris Sununu (R).
Earned bachelor's and master's degrees in mechanical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1986 and 1987) and an MBA from Harvard (1991).
Career experience before Congress included engineering, consulting and manufacturing work and running operations at an electronics company.
Won the open 1st District U.S. House seat in 1996 by defeating Democrat Joe Keefe, and was re-elected in 1998 and 2000; he served on the House Appropriations and Budget committees.
Elected to the U.S. Senate in 2002 after defeating incumbent Sen. Bob Smith in the Republican primary and Gov. Jeanne Shaheen in the general election; Shaheen defeated him in a 2008 rematch.

After leaving the Senate, served as a faculty member at St. Anselm College and as a director at Boston Scientific, joined the law firm Akin Gump as an adjunct senior policy advisor in 2010, and was named to Lloyd's of London's governing council in 2019.
Announced his 2026 campaign in late 2025, received President Trump's endorsement, and won the September 8, 2026 Republican primary with 68.4% of the vote over Scott Brown (26.4%).
